title: Doctors who ‘deny’ image-adoration mean only absolute latria—they still allow the relative honor the Councils sanction
source_text: XXX. Quod spectat Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, videntur quidam eorum contraria docere iis quae ab istius Ecclesiae Conciliis definita jam ostendimus. Sunt enim qui simpliciter negant adorandas esse imagines, & clamant sibi per calumniam objici, quod Imagines Christi & Sanctorum adorent, ut fuit jam supra a nobis observatum. Cum tamen Ecclesiae Romanae Concilia, nempe Nicenum secundum & Constantinopolitanum, quod octavum Generale vocant, a Concilio Tridentino probata, anathemate sanxerint imaginibus esse deferendam adorationem. Verum mens istorum Doctorum non est Concilia jam dicta damnare, aut ab eorum doctrina ullo modo recedere. Etenim quum imagines negant esse adorandas, istud intelligunt de adoratione summa & absoluta, qua adoratur aliquid tanquam summus finis, & primum principium, ac omnis boni primarius author, quam adorationem soli Deo deberi agnoscunt; non vero de adoratione relativa, vel inferiori, qua imagines coli posse non negant, & quam solam etiam imaginibus tribuendam esse, Ecclesiae Romanae Concilia sanciunt.
pass_a_gloss: As for the Doctors of the Roman Church, some of them seem to teach things contrary to what we have already shown defined by that Church’s Councils. For there are those who simply deny that images are to be adored, and cry that it is objected to them by calumny that they adore the Images of Christ and of the Saints, as was already observed by us above. Yet the Councils of the Roman Church—namely the second Nicene and the Constantinopolitan which they call the eighth General, approved by the Council of Trent—have sanctioned by anathema that adoration is to be paid to images. But the mind of those Doctors is not to condemn the Councils already named, or to withdraw in any way from their doctrine. For when they deny that images are to be adored, they understand that of the supreme and absolute adoration by which something is adored as the highest end and first principle and primary author of every good, which adoration they acknowledge is owed to God alone; not of the relative or inferior adoration by which they do not deny that images can be cultivated, and which alone also the Councils of the Roman Church sanction as to be attributed to images.
pass_b_english: Some Roman doctors ‘deny’ image-adoration and cry calumny—yet Nicaea II, Constantinople VIII, and Trent anathematize refusal to adore images.
Their escape: they deny only absolute latria to images, while still allowing the Councils’ relative honor-cult.

choices.why: Absolute-vs-relative distinction reconciles deniers with Councils.
